s02-activation.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected 05cbecc. S02-F1: `an_adapter_switched_during_a_frame_gets_only_frames_it_covered` drives the test window's adapter from inside a render through the new test-support `TestAccessibilityAdapter` (`VisualTestContext::accessibility_adapter`), drawing frames by hand with draw-on-flush off: a frame the adapter joins mid-draw sends nothing and the next sends the full tree; a frame it leaves mid-draw sends nothing, nor does the next. The deactivation half fails under the `!self.shadow && self.platform_this_frame` mutation (coordinator ran it) and the activation half guards an end-flag-only rule. S02-F2: `child_reads_the_environment` (child process with GPUX_ACCESSIBILITY = always/off/auto/loud) now asserts `Application::on_test_platform(..).with_accessibility_mode(mode).accessibility_mode() == mode` for every mode and that an app without the builder reads the variable; `on_test_platform` is cfg(test/test-support), `Application::accessibility_mode` is a plain getter. Reran `cargo test -p gpux --test a11y_activation`: 13 passed. The devtools_snapshot_tree.rs deletion is explained (coverage moved to s05's `semantic_query_accesskit`), outside s02's criteria.
s02-activation.summaryMarkdown: Implementation of s02 matches the design on reading: `A11y` splits the platform flag, the shared inspection count and the app-wide `AccessibilityMode`; `sync_active_flag` samples them at frame start; the send rule checks the platform flag at start and end; `Off` masks only the platform source and sends one root-only tree to an exposed adapter (`end_platform_frame`), leaving `Off` sends a full tree; `new_inaccessible` refuses every source and yields a disabled guard; the first guard forgets a stale tree and forces a refresh (deferred to after the draw when started mid-draw), the last drop requests a frame; `a11y_tree` reads `A11yDebug`'s retained update. The wasm gate around `a11y_init` is gone, the web host exports `startA11yInspection`/`a11yTree` and the lane B spec reads the buttons; the `accessibility` features gate `accesskit_macos/windows/unix` cleanly with `wayland`/`x11` no longer pulling `accesskit_unix`. The mobile adapter cargo-tree half of ACT-5 is deferred to s05b's planned check, which is consistent with the plan. Two minor test gaps keep the review failed: the platform half of the mid-frame send rule (S02-F1) and builder-over-env precedence (S02-F2) are not exercised by the check's test group. Outside s02's criteria: commit 756f8f2 also deletes `crates/gpui/tests/devtools_snapshot_tree.rs` while the devtools snapshot API it covered still exists (removal belongs to s09); the coordinator should confirm that was intended.

F2: `scroll_a11y_node_into_view` clamps to the context's per-axis max, uses `ScrollHandle::scroll_to` for handles, writes untracked offsets plus `note_scrolled_by_id` (same bookkeeping as `note_scrolled`, keyed by the global id `painted_container` remembers), notifies the painting views and no longer calls `refresh()`; new test checks a cached sibling view is not re-rendered. F3: value is the display projection and `PerGrapheme` yields `Role::PasswordInput`; new test asserts only the mask is exposed. F4: Click falls back only when the last tree's node advertises Click (`last_tree` is captured in release builds too), Blur returns false with nothing focused; test asserts both on `Inert`. check --sprint s03-tree passed 4/4 at this snapshot.
s03-tree.summaryMarkdown: TREE-1/3/4 behave as specified apart from the findings: Label leaves for `&str`/`SharedString`/`StyledText` with per-parent ordinals and AccessKit name-from-contents, `InteractiveText`/`Text` with ids keep their own Label nodes, the id map exists only while inspecting, relations resolve in order and drop unknown ids, custom actions are listed and dispatched by id, and `perform_a11y_action` shares the adapter's dispatch path. Failed on four findings: leaf ids change when inspection toggles (breaks TREE-2's equal screen-reader view; confirmed with a removed probe test), ScrollIntoView forces a whole-window refresh and writes untracked offsets directly, masked text fields leak their source text, and the Click/Blur fallbacks return true without a handler.

s04-fast.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected 61e623f. `A11y::open_bounds` is pushed in `push_element` for hidden and shown nodes and popped by `pop_node` into the `Push` event; the only callers (`element.rs` prepaint and `A11y::replay`) push and pop it in step, `begin_frame` clears it, and `set_visual_bounds` updates the open entry and a shown node's `node_bounds`. New lane C `a_list_of_controls_carries_where_actions_reach_its_rows` (Content::Controls: id'd focusable Button rows with click and Increment handlers) compares the whole renumbered a11y description incl. focusables, listeners and `a11y bounds ... scroll` lines through a scroll down and back; it fails at step 3 when `pop_node` reads the shown-only `node_bounds` again (seeded, restored). New `a_reused_view_carries_its_active_descendant_relations_and_synthetic_children` fails when the ActiveDescendant replay arm is skipped (seeded, restored). Both groups pass at the current snapshot (lane C 5/5, a11y_retention 9/9).
s04-fast.summaryMarkdown: The event-log design is sound and integrated on every reuse path: `reuse_prepaint`/`reuse_paint` replay events and move listeners, retained shifted indices and splice stretches carry `a11y_events_index`/`a11y_listeners_index`, `transact` checkpoints and rolls back, the frame swap double-buffers events and listeners, a source turning on forces a full draw, the view/retained/layer/verify bypasses and the `Accessibility` bypass reason are gone, and shadow verification builds its own tree (running `check-fast-a11y-describe` with `--features diagnostics` is right, since the shadow test only exists there). Seeding a dropped `replay_offset` fails all four lane C tests. One real defect: list rows first prepainted while held off screen replay with zero-size action bounds once shown (S04-F1), which the lane C group cannot see because it compares only AccessKit node fields over rows without ids. The active-descendant, relation and synthetic-child replay arms have no test (S04-F2).

The last matches `layers/reuse.rs:104-107` (`a11y.replay_offset = step`). `git grep -i devkit` in the file is empty. `docs/fast-mode.md:344` no longer has the hitbox-count clause. `.agentx/memory/knowledge/gpui/rules.md:20` now says gpui has no `rayx_diagnostics` alias and that `gpui_web`/`gpui_wgpu` keep one, which matches the manifests. s09-removal.summaryMarkdown: The removal itself is sound. Every retired symbol, the `devtools` feature, the `DEVTOOLS` gate, the per-element records and paint-time text semantics, the DevKit-node handling in fast mode and the pointer-semantics scope are gone. Nothing outside the DevKit read the deleted data: `hidden_hitboxes` and `NodeRow` only fed DevKit hitbox counts and snapshot order, and the verifier still compares the accessibility tree and now the effect counts. The guard covers types, methods, frame records, the gate and the Cargo feature, and both its scans can fail. `Window::effect_diagnostics()` is the old effect snapshot's computation field for field, and `effect_diagnostics.rs` exercises each count. RayX 3716df72 restores `navigation_region_view_paints_configured_screen_effect_region` exactly as it was before the epic, plus the region count in `inherits_default_transition`. No RayX feature enabled gpui's dropped `rayx_diagnostics` alias. The upstream checklist, `docs/fast-mode.md` (the `devtools` section), README, LINUX-WSL and the gpux memory sync are accurate. Checks passed 3/3, and lane A passed 119/0 (`s09-lane-a.log`). Failing only on stale DevKit wording left in `docs/upstream/gpui-fast.md`, one `fast-mode.md` clause and one gpui memory rule.

s10-after.deltaSummaryMarkdown: Inspected gpux 619a011 and 6db56e2. The setup note now names the browser list scrolls' two CPU levels, with the per-repetition figures, and leaves those two scenarios out of the browser ranges while keeping their cells in the tables. I recomputed the ranges from the raw medians. Browser c′/a′ without the list scrolls is 0.90× (`dashboard-clock` 1.207/1.348) to 1.48× (`table-stream`). Browser i′/a′ without them is 1.10× (`dashboard-all-panels`) to 1.87× (`scroll-div-cards`). macOS i′/a′ is 0.94–1.44×. The examples now match the tables and name their target: macOS 0.62 → 0.89 and 1.68 → 2.38 ms, browser 1.29 → 1.83 and 2.16 → 4.04 ms. The "unexplained" wording is replaced by the two-level cause. 6db56e2 records the macOS first-frame hang (no `CVDisplayLink` subscription; about 5 of 200 epic-binary launches against 0 of 78 for b) as an open follow-up in `.agentx/memory/knowledge/platform/desktop/state.md`. The change is docs and memory only; there are no checks.
s10-after.summaryMarkdown: Every other part of PERF-2 holds up under the raw reports. All 4×66 reports are fast mode on (`FastMode { layout_retention, view_retention, splice, scroll_layers: true }`) with no inactive frames, and `a11y_nodes` is set only in c′, so the switch took effect. (1) a′ vs b: I recomputed the per-repetition CPU and `draw` p50 of the same-session control from `control-a`/`control-b`. The ranges overlap on every scenario on both targets (repetition spread is ±20–40%, so CPU alone could not resolve a ~10–20% change), and the allocation counts and bytes per frame are identical to within 1–6 allocations. That is the decisive evidence that a′ does no extra per-frame work, so "no regression above the noise" is supported. Using the same-session b instead of the day-earlier before-b is right given the 1.05–1.42× drift. (2) c′: the medians match the doc (CPU 0.96–1.34× on macOS; allocations 1.3–33×). The named cause is well supported: the extra allocations scale at about 7 per tree node on every scenario (dashboard-clock +6,095 for 868 nodes, scroll-div-cards +19,580 for 2,801, text-typing +1,071 for 151). The browser list-scroll drop (c′ faster in 2 of 3 repetitions) is honestly reported as unexplained, and it is not a regression. (3) The live-heap deltas match the medians; values ≤0.1 MB sit within repetition spread. (4) The hang sample shows the main thread blocked in the AppKit run loop with no display-link thread. The pre-existing claim rests on the before-(a) `table-stream` timeout in a 58257fe build, which is plausible but indirect; running `hang/loop.sh` against the wt-b binary would settle it. Failing only on the tree-size table, which was measured without inspection.

s10a-voiceover-fixes.summaryMarkdown:
**Fork scope.** The fork is within CLAUDE.md's rules on the wgpu precedent. d3ff359's `src/` is byte-identical to crates.io `accesskit_macos-0.27.1` (diff -r), and its manifest is the published normalized one with only the package name, version (`0.27.1-gpux.1`), description and repository changed. The workspace keeps the Rust name through `package = "gpux-accesskit-macos"` with an exact path+version dependency: no `[patch]`, no git dependency, and the lockfile holds one `accesskit` (0.25.1). CLAUDE.md, the README and docs/upstream document the fork and its removal path.

**Fork changes (5fbb6a2).** Every change is marked `gpux fork:` and stays within d-macos-adapter-fork: table rows and row/cell index ranges, `isAccessibilityExpanded` plus `AXExpandedChanged`, `accessibilityValueDescription` for range roles, refusing `setAccessibilityValue:` where increment/decrement exists, and allowing press on disabled controls. That last change is safe: `press()` still sends Click only when the node is clickable, and gpux advertises Click only for elements with click listeners, so a disabled control without a handler does nothing. The slider default is the ARIA one, with `a11y_aria_defaults`. The lane D check reads the real NSAccessibility surface in process and fails on each property.

**Web (e521be1).** `place_after` keeps focus: it re-focuses if the move blurred the element, the window-level blur listener is unaffected, and mirror listeners ignore events whose target is the textarea, so keys go through the textarea's own path once. The fixed-position textarea's containing block becomes the mirror root's transform, which only moves its 1px box to the canvas origin. Moving the textarea mid-composition on a reorder is possible but rare. The attribute/style skips are covered by a MutationObserver spec that fails without them, and the fixed walk passes Details to the end of the page, which supports the cause.

**One gap.** The walkthrough record overstates the web results (the finding). Separately, outside this sprint: RayX's decision `2026-08-08-ui-accessibility-component-accesskit-contract` ("leave WASM accessibility unsupported") is still `status: current`; the design declares it superseded, so the epic's closing memory promotion should mark it.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: Now: three of four scroll scenarios allocate fewer bytes in (c); `scroll-div-cards` 1.15x macOS / 1.14x web; `scroll-variable-list` macOS heap 17.8 -> 19.6 MB. Matches the tables.
Now 1.9-6.2x; macOS (c)/(b) CPU ratios over the fast-mode scenarios are 1.93-6.17.
Setup paragraph now explains macOS dirty-to-present latency snaps to ~4/8 ms frame steps at 120 Hz, so the (a)/(b) halvings and 1.5x jumps are one step, not work.
Now states the timeout per log-a.txt, gives the `ps` CPU reading as an observation, and says the cause was not established.
Resolved: the clone and clear-and-set tests now cover every property gpux writes, including the `disabled` flag and the `invalid` enum it clears and sets again.

**Platform half of the mid-frame rule is untested.** Expected (ACT-1, d-activation-sources invariant): updates reach `PlatformWindow::a11y_tree_update` only when the platform flag covered the frame's start *and* end, and the `a11y_activation` group can fail if either half is dropped. Observed: `A11y::platform_covers_frame_end` (`crates/gpui/src/window/a11y.rs`) does check the live flag at frame end, but every platform activation/deactivation in `crates/gpui/tests/a11y_activation.rs` happens between frames; the only mid-frame switch (`a_source_switched_during_a_frame_takes_effect_on_the_next`) changes the mode, which by design is sampled at frame start. Replacing the body with `!self.shadow && self.platform_this_frame` (or reading only the end-of-frame flag) passes the whole group. Repair: add a test in the `a11y_activation` group (selectable by that name) that flips the platform flag during a frame both ways - deactivation inside render (frame built, nothing sent, nothing sent next frame) and activation inside render (nothing sent for that frame, full tree on the activation's refresh). Either expose a test-support hook reachable from render (e.g. a `TestAppContext`/`Window` test helper that calls the stored `A11yCallbacks` deactivation/activation) or add in-crate unit tests in `a11y.rs` named `a11y_activation_*` that drive `sync_active_flag` / `platform_covers_frame_end` / `end_platform_frame` with a controlled `Arc<AtomicBool>`, and include them in `check-a11y-activation`'s selection. Seed the mutation above to prove the test fails.

**Builder-over-variable precedence is not proven by the check's group.** Expected (ACT-2, check-a11y-activation description "GPUX_ACCESSIBILITY values and builder precedence"): a test shows `Application::with_accessibility_mode` wins over `GPUX_ACCESSIBILITY`. Observed: the child-process test `child_reads_the_environment` only shows that a later `App::set_accessibility_mode` wins; the builder is tested only by the in-crate unit test `a11y_activation_builder_sets_the_application_mode` (`crates/gpui/src/window/a11y.rs`), which runs with the variable unset and is not run by `cargo test -p gpux --test a11y_activation`. Repair: in the child process (variable set, e.g. `always`), build an application with `with_accessibility_mode(AccessibilityMode::Off)` on the test platform and assert its mode is `Off` (add a small test-support accessor if `Application` exposes no mode getter), or move the builder test under the env-child harness; make `check-a11y-activation` run it (or add its `--lib a11y_activation` selection to the check).

**Text-leaf ids change when inspection starts or stops.** Expected (TREE-2, d-text-leaves): the screen-reader view of a frame with inspection containers equals the view without them, and a leaf id changes only when the order of the text changes. Observed: `A11yNodeBuilder::push_text_leaf` hashes `ids_stack.last()` and the ordinal in `text_ordinals.last()`, and `push` gives every inspection `GenericContainer` its own stack entry and ordinal scope, so every leaf under or after an id-only element gets a different id while inspecting. A probe (root view > `div().id("box").child("Inside")` + `"After"`, platform source on) gave `After` #8891427454842729713 / `Inside` #9369559791910956854 without inspection and #12541788937870955646 / #2105994981808584525 with it. AccessKit adapters key platform objects by NodeId, so an agent starting inspection replaces every such leaf under a running screen reader. `screen_readers_see_the_same_tree_with_and_without_containers` compares only role/label/value, so it cannot see this. Repair: derive a leaf's id and ordinal from the nearest non-container node (containers do not open an ordinal scope; keep the owner id and counter on a separate stack that skips containers), keep the leaf's tree parent as is, and make the screen-reader-view test compare node ids (and focus id) of the filtered tree, plus a leaf after an id-only sibling.

**ScrollIntoView is not an ordinary scroll.** Expected (d-actions invariant, positioning-scroll rules): offsets are published only where scroll owners publish them today, so scroll layers see an ordinary scroll. Observed: `Window::scroll_a11y_node_into_view` writes a handle-less div's `Rc<RefCell<Point>>` directly (no `fast::layers::invalidate::note_scrolled`, no owner notify, unclamped) and ends with `self.refresh()`, which sets `refreshing` and draws the whole window from scratch, dropping every scroll layer's record (`policy::forget_content`) and bypassing view/paint retention on every ScrollIntoView, for tracked handles too (`ScrollHandle::scroll_to` already bumps `fast_version`). The test passes only because of the full refresh. Repair: for handles rely on `scroll_to` plus a plain frame request (dirty the window / notify the owner view without `refresh`); for handle-less divs record the owner view and fast container with the scroll target and go through the wheel listener's path (`note_scrolled` + `cx.notify(owner)`, clamped to the scroll max); add a fast-mode test (`fast_mode_a11y` or `a11y_actions`) asserting a ScrollIntoView keeps the scroll layer (no `forget_content`, ordinary-scroll counters) and that the frame equals the from-scratch oracle.

**Masked text fields expose their plain text.** Expected: a field drawn with `EditableTextDisplayTransform::PerGrapheme` (password masking) exposes no source text to screen readers or inspection (the tree feeds the devtools sidecar). Observed: `EditableText::render` (`editable_text/element.rs`) sets `aria_value(state.text())` with role `TextInput`/`MultilineTextInput` regardless of `display_transform`, so the secret is in `accesskit::Node::value`, in `Window::a11y_tree`, and in semantic queries' value matching. Repair: when the transform is `PerGrapheme`, use `Role::PasswordInput` and either omit the value or set the masked display text (one mask per grapheme); for `Projected`, decide and document whether the value is the projection; add a test group case asserting a masked field's node carries no source text.

**Requests without a handler still act and return true.** Expected (TREE-5): a request without a handler does nothing and returns false. Observed: in `Window::handle_a11y_action` the Click fallback synthesizes a mouse down/up at the centre of any node with recorded bounds and returns true, even for a node that advertises no Click (e.g. the test's `Inert` Label), and can fire whatever click handler lies under it; `Blur` returns true when nothing is focused. Repair: synthesize Click only for a node whose last-frame node advertises `Action::Click` (else return false), return false from Blur when nothing is focused, and add the `Inert` Click case to `handlers_run_through_perform_a11y_action`.

Resolved in 61e623f: hidden nodes' bounds travel on `open_bounds` into their `Push` event, so rows a list layer held off screen keep their action bounds when shown; guarded by the lane C controls test.
Resolved in 61e623f: a reused/spliced view with an active descendant, a labelled-by relation and synthetic children is compared with a from-scratch window.

**Expected:** QRY-2 and task t12 list `ignored_hitbox_semantics` among the suites moved to the new tree: it should prove on the AccessKit tree that an element whose hitbox is `HitboxBehavior::Ignore` (out of hit testing) still keeps its accessibility node, which is the behaviour RayX's pointer detectors rely on.

**Observed:** `crates/gpui/tests/ignored_hitbox_semantics.rs` is unchanged since 41efd38 (before the epic). It is still an `include_str!` grep of `window.rs` for devtools strings (`DevtoolsPointerAction`, `with_pointer_semantics_suppressed`, `semantics.pointer_actions.clear()`). It reads no tree, so it proves nothing about the new tree, and it will break or be deleted when decision 5 removes pointer actions. Nothing else checks that ignored hitboxes keep their AccessKit nodes.

**Repair:** Rewrite `ignored_hitbox_semantics.rs` as a behavioural test. Render an element with an id, a role and a label inside a custom element that inserts a `HitboxBehavior::Ignore` hitbox over it. Locate it with `semantic_query` (role/name/id, bounds in window pixels). Assert that a locator click at its bounds reaches whatever is under it, not the ignored hitbox. Drop the devtools source-string asserts. Seed the failure (skip the node for ignored hitboxes) to show the test can fail.

findings.descriptionMarkdown:
**Android adapter is a set-once static that outlives its Activity and view.**

Expected: the mobile rules say *never keep per-activity Android state in a set-once static: a restarted `android_main` in the same process must replace it*, and `d-mobile-adapters` requires the adapter to be dropped before the view it is attached to. `jni.rs` already replaces `ANDROID_APP`/`PLATFORM` per run (`Current<T>`), and the embedded host's `shutdown()`/`initialize()` swap the Activity.

Observed: `crates/gpui_mobile/src/android/accessibility.rs` creates `ADAPTER` once (`if adapter.is_none()`) on the first Activity's decor view / SurfaceView and never drops or replaces it; `Registration::drop` only removes the window, and `WINDOWS.activated` is never reset. After a NativeActivity restart in the same process (which CI's lane E emulator does at startup, per the `Current` comment) or an embedded Activity recreation, new windows register with the stale adapter: its host is a weak ref to the dead view, the new view gets no delegate, and TalkBack sees nothing. The old view and its delegate are never uninstalled.

Repair: tie the adapter to the Activity/host it was built on: record the host (or Activity) it was created for and, in `register`, drop and recreate it (resetting `activated`) when `activity_as_ptr()`/the host view differs; drop it (its `Drop` uninstalls the delegate on the UI thread) when the last registration goes and on `clear_embedded_context`/activity destroy. Add a lane E or focused check that proves a second adapter is installed on the new host after the adapter is recreated (e.g. close all windows, reopen, re-dump), so the path can fail.

**Embedded host view lookup guesses, off the UI thread, and can panic the UI thread.**

Expected: the adapter sits on the view GPUI draws into. gpux already has the declaration of that view for embedded hosts whose SurfaceView does not fill the window: `dev.gpux.mobile.Composition.setHostView`.

Observed: `host_view` ignores it and takes the first `SurfaceView` found depth-first under `android.R.id.content` (an app with a video/camera SurfaceView before GPUI's gets the wrong host and wrong bounds), and walks the view hierarchy (`getDecorView`, `getChildAt`) from the GPUI thread rather than the UI thread. `InjectingAdapter::new` panics on the UI thread (`host already has an accessibility delegate`) if the consumer set a delegate on that view. The embedded path has no runtime proof (lane E runs the NativeActivity host only).

Repair: prefer the view named through `Composition.setHostView` (expose it to Rust, or let the embedded host pass its SurfaceView to `initialize`), fall back to the SurfaceView search/decor view; check `getAccessibilityDelegate()` first and log-and-skip instead of letting the adapter panic; document in `docs/accessibility.md` that the embedded host's view is chosen this way.

**Known limits omit the Android one-window behaviour.**

Expected (SR-6): what each platform's screen reader gets and its known limits.

Observed: `docs/accessibility.md` (Android, Known limits) does not say that one adapter serves every GPUI window on the Activity's surface and TalkBack sees only the front (last opened) window, nor that a window behind it is unreachable until the front closes; the iOS section does not say each window's Metal view is separate.

Repair: add both to the Android/iOS sections or Known limits (and the restart behaviour once S05B-F1 is fixed).

**testkit: `a11y_dump` was inserted under `screenshot`'s doc comment, and the new request has no parse test.**

Expected: each function keeps its own rustdoc; new testkit requests are covered like `tap`/`swipe`/`trim-memory` in `tooling/testkit/tests/android.rs`.

Observed: in `tooling/testkit/src/android.rs` the `/// Takes screenshot number …` paragraph now sits directly above `/// uiautomator dump …` on `fn a11y_dump`, so `a11y_dump` carries both docs and `fn screenshot` has none; `request("gpux-conformance-host: a11y-dump 3")` is not tested.

Repair: move the screenshot paragraph back above `fn screenshot`, and add `Request::A11yDump` parse cases (valid number, missing number) to the existing request test.

**Spec text no longer matches the chosen Android design.**

Expected: the design and the criterion describe what was built.

Observed: `d-mobile-adapters` says *one adapter per window* and SR-5/the design say the adapter goes on *the NativeActivity's content view*. The implementation (reasonably, since a view takes one delegate and all windows share the Activity's surface) installs one shared adapter on the decor view (whose coordinates are the NativeActivity surface's) serving the front window.

Repair: the coordinator amends `d-mobile-adapters` (one adapter per Android host view, serving the front window; the decor view for a NativeActivity) and the SR-5 wording, so the final review measures the real contract.

**Closing the last window and opening another on the same Activity leaves TalkBack with no adapter (race introduced by the F1/F2 repairs).**

Expected: SR-5/`d-mobile-adapters` — the adapter is dropped with the last window and a later window on the surface gets the tree again.

Observed: `Registration::drop` (`accessibility_registry.rs`) drops the `InjectingAdapter` when the last window goes; its `Drop` only *posts* `uninstall_delegate` to the UI thread (`attach_and_post_to_ui_thread`). The next `register` on the same host runs `create()` synchronously on the GPUI thread (not the UI thread, in both the NativeActivity and the embedded host), and the new pre-check `getAccessibilityDelegate()` still sees the old `dev.accesskit.android.Delegate` because the posted uninstall has not run yet; `create` logs "already has an accessibility delegate" and returns `None`, so the window registers with no adapter and TalkBack sees nothing until another window opens. (Without the pre-check, AccessKit's own install would run after the queued uninstall and succeed.) The registry tests use a fake adapter and lane E keeps the anchor window open, so nothing exercises this.

Repair: treat AccessKit's own delegate as ours — skip the warning when the existing delegate `is_instance_of` `dev.accesskit.android.Delegate` (load it through the adapter's class loader, or compare class names), or move the check into a UI-thread post; alternatively keep the adapter while the host is unchanged and drop it only on a host change or `release()`. Add a check that can fail: e.g. in lane E close every GPUI window including the anchor (or a focused registry/host test that reopens on the same host) and re-dump to find the scene's nodes.

**`wait` panics in the browser.** `requests::wait` (`crates/gpux_devtools/src/requests.rs`, `use std::time::{Duration, Instant}` and `let start = Instant::now()`) uses `std::time::Instant`, which panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` ("time not implemented on this platform"); gpui itself uses `web-time`/`scheduler::Instant` there. Expected: DEV-5's crate "builds for wasm32" and the web transport serve the browser, so every request must also run there. Observed: `check-devtools-web-build` only compiles, and the first `wait` from a sidecar would abort the page's app. The timeout is also measured in wall time while its 16 ms poll runs on the executor's clock, so the two clocks disagree on the test platform.
**Repair:** measure the start and timeout with the executor's clock (`cx.background_executor().now()`, the `scheduler::Instant` gpui uses), or `web_time::Instant` on wasm, and drop `std::time::Instant` from the crate. Add a test that times `wait` out by advancing only the test executor's clock (no real-time sleep), so the timeout follows the executor's clock.

**The web transport's socket lifecycle leaks and throws.** In `transport/web.rs`, (a) `Transport` has no `Drop` (`Control::Shutdown` is `allow(dead_code)` on wasm), so a second `install`, which the docs say "replaces the earlier connection", drops `State` without closing its `web_sys::WebSocket`: the old connection stays open to the sidecar and its handlers are dropped closures; (b) `close()` leaves the old socket's handlers attached, and an off-then-on toggle before the browser fires `close` makes `connect()` replace `state.handlers`, so the old socket's `onclose` calls a dropped `Closure` (a wasm-bindgen exception). If the closure were kept alive instead, it would `take()` the *new* socket. (c) `onclose` after a failed connect counts as `was_open` because the socket is stored before it opens, so every failed retry sends a spurious `Disconnected`.
**Repair:** on close, detach `onopen`/`onmessage`/`onclose` (set them to `None`) before `socket.close()` and before dropping the closures; tag each socket with a generation so a stale event cannot act on a newer socket; record `open` on `onopen`; add `impl Drop for Transport` that closes the socket. The native transport handles the same cases correctly.

**Answers can reach a later connection.** `received` spawns each request's answer and sends it whenever it completes (`cx.update(|cx| send(cx, Message::response(Some(id), outcome)))`). A `wait` or `longPress` in flight when the sidecar restarts answers on the *next* connection, possibly before or interleaved with that connection's own ids (a fresh sidecar starts its ids again). The native thread also keeps `Control::Send`s queued while disconnected and drains them on the new socket before the foreground's `hello`, so the app's first message on a connection can be a stale response, against DEV-2's "first message is `hello`". `connected()` also does not check `enabled`, so an `Event::Connected` already queued when `set_enabled(false)` runs takes guards and sends `hello` for a moment.
**Repair:** give each connection a generation (incremented on `Connected`/`Disconnected`), capture it with each spawned answer, and drop answers whose generation is over; have the native thread discard queued `Send`s when a connection ends; ignore `Connected` while `!enabled`. Cover the restart with a test in `connection.rs` (an open `wait`, the server dropped and re-accepted: the first frame is `hello` and the old id never arrives).

**Several input kinds are tested without checking their effect.** In `tests/actions.rs`, `input_drags_wheels_pinches_and_long_presses` asserts only that `drag`, `pinch` and `longPress` return `ok`, and `input_clicks_double_clicks_and_hovers` checks nothing about `hover`. Deleting the `dispatch_event` calls for those kinds would leave the group green, so the check cannot fail for them (the repository rule: "a check must be able to fail"). Only click, wheel, type and press have an observed outcome.
**Repair:** give `Controls` listeners that record the drag's move with the pressed button (or an `on_drag`/`on_drag_move`), a pinch (`on_pinch`), a hover (`.hover` style or `on_hover`) and a long press (the touch recognizer's long-press, or the touch `Started`/`Ended` pair after `durationMs`), and assert each in the status line.

**`stats` has no frame count without `diagnostics`.** DEV-5 says `stats` returns frame counts, fast-mode counters and the tree's size. Observed: with the crate's default features `fast` is `null` and nothing counts frames (`observe.rs` asserts `stats["fast"].is_null()`), so an agent on a default build gets only `treeNodes`. Fast mode's counters are rightly `diagnostics`-only (a gpui rule), but a frame count is not a diagnostics collector.
**Repair:** report a frame count in every build. Either the window exposes a cheap drawn-frame counter, or the crate counts frames only while connected with an `on_next_frame` chain started on connect and dropped on disconnect (nothing per frame while disconnected). If the owner wants frame counts only with `diagnostics`, amend DEV-5 to say so.

**Text content is written into the YAML unescaped.** `snapshot::write` appends a `text` node's content raw after `: ` (`out.push_str(&content)`), so text with a newline, a leading `-`/`[`/`"`, or `: ` makes the snapshot invalid YAML or gives it another structure, unlike Playwright's aria snapshot, which quotes such values. Values and names are quoted.
**Repair:** quote text content when YAML needs it (newline, a leading indicator character, `: `, ` #`, surrounding whitespace), as Playwright's `yamlEscapeValueIfNeeded` does. Add a `snapshot.rs` case with multi-line and `key: value`-like text that a YAML parser reads back as the same string.

**`type` with `replace` picks select-all by `cfg!(target_os)` and has no test.** The repair added `replace: true` to `input` `type` (`requests.rs`: `if cfg!(target_os = "macos") { "cmd-a" } else { "ctrl-a" }`). The web rules say keyboard conventions are decided through `KeyboardOs::current()`, never `cfg!(target_os = ...)`, because a wasm32 build says nothing about the visitor's keyboard: a Mac visitor in the browser gets `ctrl-a`, which does not select all, so the old text stays and the new text is added to it. No test in `actions.rs` uses `replace`, against the constraint that every new behaviour gets a test.
**Repair:** build the select-all keystroke from the secondary modifier (`Modifiers::secondary_key()` / `KeyboardOs::current()`, the way gpui names the secondary key) instead of `cfg!`. Add an `actions.rs` test that types into the Title field, types again with `replace: true`, and asserts the value is only the new text.

`initialize` advertises `capabilities.tools.listChanged: true` (crates/gpux_devtools_mcp/src/mcp.rs:57), but nothing in the crate ever writes `notifications/tools/list_changed`: `mcp::serve` (mcp.rs:12-30) only writes answers to stdin lines, and no code subscribes to `Registry` events for the MCP side. Expected: when an app connects or disconnects and the set of extension tools changes, the harness is told, as docs/devtools.md:108 promises ("the sidecar may start before or after the apps"). Observed: a harness such as Claude Code lists tools once after `initialize`, normally before any app has connected, so advertised tools like `rayx_metadata` never show up in it. The extensions.rs tests can't catch this because they call `tools/list` again after connecting. Repair: let `serve` share its writer (Arc<Mutex<W>>) with a thread subscribed to `Registry::subscribe()`, and emit `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/tools/list_changed"}` whenever a connect or disconnect changes the extension-tool names. Add an extensions.rs test that runs `mcp::serve` over a pipe (or the binary with `--port 0`) and asserts the notification line after a scripted app connects and after it disconnects.

MCP-1 lists the `browser_*` tools RayX's sidecar offered with "`browser_set_property` becomes SetValue", and d-mcp-sidecar's rationale is to keep "the tool surface agents already use" (RayX's `.claude/skills/rayx/references/devkit.md` uses `browser_set_property`). Observed: the tool is gone (crates/gpux_devtools_mcp/src/tools.rs:59-317), and stdio_protocol.rs:68-71 asserts that it is absent ("SetValue replaces it"), so agents have to switch to `gpux_act action=setValue`. Expected: `browser_set_property` (target/ref plus value) forwarded as `act` with `action: "setValue"`, answering with `### Result`, `### Ran Playwright code`, `### Page` and `### Snapshot` like the other browser tools. Repair: add the tool, replace the absence assertion with a call that checks `app.last("act")` is `setValue` with the value and that the sections are there, and document it in docs/devtools.md:135-136. If the owner meant the tool to be removed, amend MCP-1's wording with that recorded decision instead.

MCP-2 requires that "a call to a disconnected app fails naming it" in the extension-tool group. Observed (a temporary probe test, since removed): after `lab` disconnects, `tools/call rayx_metadata` with no `app` fails with `unknown tool: rayx_metadata` (tools.rs:513-515), which does not name the app. extensions.rs:86-110 only checks `gpux_snapshot` with an explicit `app`, and no test covers an app that disconnects while an `extension.call` is still pending, which is the `RequestError::Disconnected(label)` drain at apps.rs:429-433 and d-protocol's "nothing is retried after a lost response". Repair: keep the names of apps that offered each extension tool after they disconnect (for example a small map from tool name to the last offering app ids in `Registry`), so the error reads "rayx_metadata: the app lab disconnected". In extensions.rs, add (a) an extension call without `app` after disconnect that asserts the message names `lab`, and (b) a scripted app that drops the connection on receiving `extension.call`, asserting the error names `lab`, keeps the MCP request id, and that the app received the request exactly once.

`tools::call` sends every name that starts with `browser_` to `browser()` (tools.rs:491), and that function answers `unknown tool` for any name it doesn't know (tools.rs:967). `list()` (tools.rs:321-355), though, lists any non-builtin extension name. Observed (temporary probe): an app that advertises `browser_set_property` sees it in `tools/list`, but calling it fails with `unknown tool: browser_set_property`. This is the natural workaround RayX would reach for under s07-browser-set-property-dropped. Repair: dispatch to the builtins by exact name (`builtin()` names) and send every other name to `extension()`, or refuse reserved `gpux_`/`browser_` prefixes at `hello` and leave them out of the list. Add a case to extensions.rs.

The tool schemas and docs/devtools.md don't match what the app accepts. (1) `gpux_act`'s enum (tools.rs:96) leaves out `blur`, which the app supports (gpux_devtools/src/requests.rs:209) and docs/devtools.md:123 lists. The custom action is taken as `id` or `customAction` (requests.rs:239-240), but the schema has only `customAction`, and the docs say `id`. (2) `gpux_input`'s schema has `additionalProperties: false` (tools.rs:26) but no `durationMs` (longPress) and no `replace` (type), both documented at docs/devtools.md:124, so a client that validates against the schema refuses them. (3) docs/devtools.md:116 says the default window is "the app's last window". The schema says first (tools.rs:47), the app uses the active window, else the first (requests.rs:71-83), and `browser_*` uses the first (tools.rs:443). (4) docs/devtools.md:180-181 says the app answers "its extension tools by name", but the request is `extension.call` with `name` (lib.rs:14). Repair: add `blur`, `id`, `durationMs` and `replace` to the schemas, and correct the three doc statements.

MCP-3 asks docs/devtools.md to document "the accessibility modes and inspection", and docs/testing.md to name the new groups. Observed: devtools.md covers the inspection guard (lines 66-70) but says nothing about `AccessibilityMode`/`GPUX_ACCESSIBILITY` and its effect on agents: `Off` still allows inspection, while `Application::new_inaccessible` makes every request fail with "the window has no accessibility tree" (requests.rs:86-92). docs/testing.md names the lane groups and selectors but not the new crate test groups `stdio_protocol` and `extensions` (only devtools.md:186-189 names them). Repair: add a short "Accessibility modes" paragraph to devtools.md (Auto/Always/Off do not affect inspection; `new_inaccessible` disables it; link to accessibility.md#activation-sources), and add `cargo test -p gpux-devtools-mcp --test stdio_protocol|extensions` to docs/testing.md's focused-test or lane-A text.

Smaller gaps in the proofs. (1) stdio_protocol.rs drives `mcp::handle_line` in process. The binary's stdio loop (`mcp::serve`, main.rs:38-42) runs only for `--print-manifest`, so line framing, flushing and notifications over a real stdio pipe are unproved. Repair: one test that spawns `CARGO_BIN_EXE_gpux-devtools-mcp --port 0`, writes `initialize` and `tools/list` lines, and reads both answers. (2) The lane F `devtools-ios` group runs the sidecar server inside the app process (ios_host/devtools.rs:20), so it does not show that a Simulator app reaches a sidecar running as a Mac process, which is the setup docs/devtools.md:81 documents.
